title: Adaptive cross-stage kernel tiling and topology adaptation for multi-GPU inference
content:
Purpose and scope
-----------------
This doc captures an experimental design for an adaptive cross-stage kernel tiling layer plus topology-aware collective adaptation aimed at reducing tail latency and improving throughput for multi-GPU LLM inference. It focuses on: tensor/pipeline parallelism interplay, placement/tiling strategies for kernels (attention, MLP, layernorm), runtime-driven NCCL/collective tuning per-request-class, and interactions with KV cache placement.

Why this problem matters (short):
- Modern inference mixes pipeline and tensor parallelism for very large models; naive static partitioning causes hotspots and tail latency spikes when request seq lengths and batch shapes vary.
- NCCL defaults are not optimal for heterogeneous node pairings (NVLink vs PCIe, different GPU generations).
- KV cache distribution and prefetch behavior dramatically change PCIe/NVLink traffic patterns; tiling strategies should consider cache locality.

High-level idea
----------------
1) Add a lightweight "kernel tiler" stage in the serving runtime that:
   - Examines an incoming request's expected compute graph (sequence length, attention masks, kv reads/writes).
   - Picks from a small set of precompiled tiling templates for each operator (e.g., attention: time-major slice, head-major slice, fused-block slice).
   - Emits placement hints for the scheduler: per-layer shard assignment, expected inter-GPU tensor sizes, and preferred collective topologies.
2) Maintain a topology capability map for each physical node pair (NVLink bandwidth, PCIe gen, hop count). Use this to select NCCL communicator trees or ring permutations that minimize cross-host hops for heavy KV sync phases.
3) Dynamically adapt per-request using short-term performance probes and lossless tracing so the system shifts templates when latency or bandwidth pressure is observed.

Design components (details)
-------------------------
A. Kernel tiling templates
- Template meta: name, supported op types, input shape constraints, expected memory working set, estimated FLOPs, estimated inter-GPU comm volume (bytes), fallback compatibility flags.
- Example templates (toy):
  - attention-time-slice: slice along sequence length, minimizes KV scatter but increases head/allreduce overhead for KV writes. Good for long sequences where KV read hotspot concentrated.
  - attention-head-slice: slice across heads, reduces allreduce on activations but can increase per-GPU memory for KV. Useful when NVLink per-GPU BW is high.
  - fused-attention-block: small blocks fused across heads+seq to maximize kernel occupancy on Ampere/A100-like GPUs. Best for short seq, high batch.
- Templates are annotated with metric footprints so the scheduler can reason about tradeoffs.

B. Topology capability map
- Collected at node bootstrap and periodically refreshed. Fields (internal map): link_type (nvlink/pcie), bw_estimate_gbps, hop_count, is_cross_host, cuda_peer_access, cuda_p2p_l3.
- Use microbenchmarks at install-time and low-traffic windows to refine numbers (bandwidth, latency).

C. Collective selection API
- A small runtime API that accepts: communicator members, heavy-phase-flag (boolean), preferred mapping (reduce-scatter first vs ring-first), and returns a communicator config: algorithm (ring/tree/nb-tree), chunking size, and permutation order.
- Heuristics:
  - If cross-host and p2p bw < threshold: prefer tree with host-level aggregation.
  - If all GPUs intra-node with NVLink and hop_count==1: ring with large chunk sizes to amortize kernel launch.

D. KV cache placement hints
- KV hints carry: expected size for this request, read-dominant vs write-dominant, preferred shard (hot- shard id), and eviction-tolerance.
- Integrate with tiler: e.g., if a template results in concentrated KV reads from GPU-0, avoid tiling that would move those reads across slow links.

E. Short-term probe loop
- For each model instance maintain a circular probe log of recent requests stratified by request-class (seq_len bucket × batch size × feature flags).
- Periodically (configurable, default 30s) replay a few representative micro-benchmarks in-band (low priority) to validate current template's perf. Metrics: latency p50/p95, aggregate inter-GPU bytes, kernel occupancy.
- If a probe shows degradation > 10% on key metric, trigger template switch or communicator reconfigure.

Integration with scheduler and allocator
--------------------------------------
- The tiler emits a preference score per template. The scheduler uses a composite cost model: local_compute_time + expected_comm_time(local topology) + kv_penalty(locality_mismatch).
- Allocator may move stages to different GPUs when slack capacity exists, but we avoid live shard rebinds mid-request. Rebinds occur on model rollout or low-traffic windows.

NCCL tuning knobs surfaced
-------------------------
- Chunk size for reduce-scatter/allreduce; tuned by template based on average inter-GPU message size.
- Algorithm preference: ring vs tree; switch when cross-host fraction > threshold.
- Communicator permutation: prefer permutations that keep heavy-communication neighbors contiguous in the ring.
- Subcommunicators: create host-local subcommunicators with host-level aggregation to reduce cross-host traffic (useful for PCIe hosts connected by RDMA).

KV considerations and cache-coherent heuristics
---------------------------------------------
- Hot-key detection: runtime tracks per-shard access frequency; hot shards should be co-located with shards frequently doing KV reads in current request-class.
- Lazy prefetch: for pipeline-parallel stages, prefetch next-layer KV across fast links only when prefetch probability > ppf_thresh. The tiler emits the probability estimate.
- Eviction policies take into account estimated recompute cost vs fetch cost (recompute = rerun upstream activations vs fetch over slow link).

Failure modes and fallbacks
--------------------------
- If a communicator reconfigure fails or regression observed, fall back to a golden-template: conservative ring with small chunk size and host-aggregation enabled.
- On GPU preemption or PCIe throttling, mark node as degraded and favor templates minimizing cross-host transfers.

Experiments plan (what to measure)
---------------------------------
Baseline experiments (compare to current static partitioning):
1) Synthetic trace: varying batch shapes and sequence length distributions (mix short/long tails). Measure p50/p90/p99 latency and tokens/sec.
2) Real workload trace replay (internal prod sample). Key metrics: tail latency, 95th-percentile inter-GPU bytes, kernel occupancy variance.
3) Failure injection: simulate NVLink drop (throttle) and measure graceful degradation.

A/B test matrix:
- A: current static tiling (control)
- B1: tiling with topology map but static template selection
- B2: tiling + probe-driven template switching
- B3: tiling + communicator-adaptation + kv-hint integration

Success criteria:
- p95 tail latency reduced by >= 12% under mixed traces for large-context models.
- Tokens/sec improved >= 8% at 95% SLO target under prober tuning.
- No increase in error rates or incorrect outputs.

Open questions / tradeoffs (callouts)
-----------------------------------
- How much CPU overhead is acceptable for per-request tiler computations? We should cap to < 500 usec on median.
- Is in-band probing acceptable for high-SLO tenants? Might need background worker.
- What is the consistency model for KV when we relocate shards? Strong consistency vs eventual in some degenerate fallbacks (need to discuss with data-plane owners).
- How to version templates and ensure backward compatibility with existing fallback chains.

Implementation milestones (rough)
--------------------------------
- M0 (2w): topology capability map collector + inspector CLI + microbench harness.
- M1 (4w): tiler framework and template registry, minimal templates (time-slice, head-slice), unit tests.
- M2 (3w): communicator selection API + NCCL glue for permutations and chunk size control.
- M3 (3w): KV hint plumbing and scheduler cost model integration.
- M4 (4w): probe loop, telemetry dashboards (tiling decisions, template switch events), and canary roll.

Implementation notes and pitfalls
-------------------------------
- Be conservative with prefetch: false-positive prefetches cause expensive PCIe transfers. Instrument and gate prefetch by bandwidth-saturation signal.
- Avoid per-token communicator reconfigure; do it at per-request or per-batch granularity.
- Some NCCL APIs are opaque; keep a golden-backed path that uses standard collective calls while incrementally exposing chunking/permutation options.

Follow-ups and who to involve
----------------------------
- SRE/observability: dashboards for inter-GPU bytes, p95 latency by template, and probe success rates.
- Platform: ensure topology map is accessible in private deployments and VPC (some features may be restricted).
- KV / storage: define eviction-recompute cost model and instrumentation.
- QA: long-run soak test with traffic mix and periodic link-throttling.

Short actionable TODOs (next 2 weeks)
-----------------------------------
- [Asha] prototype topology microbench (nvlink/pcie bandwidth/latency) and publish results for two node types. (ETA 2025-09-10)
- [Riley] implement minimal tiler registry and two templates; add unit tests for shape constraints. (ETA 2025-09-17)
- [Miguel] spike on NCCL permutation APIs and notes on which versions expose chunking controls. (ETA 2025-09-12)
- Schedule 30-min sync with KV owners to align on hot-key telemetry fields.

Notes and rough sketches
-----------------------
(put sketches later)
- ASCII bandwidth map sketch: GPU0--NVLink--GPU1 | GPU0--PCIe--Host--RDMA--Host--GPU4
- Example template JSON (sketch):
  { name: "attention-time-slice-v1", ops: ["attention"], seq_min: 8, seq_max: 8192, expected_comm_bytes: "seq_len * hidden * head_count * 2" }

Slack / context refs
-------------------
- this is a sibling effort to ENG-1102 (activation-paging) but focused on real-time tiling + collective adaptation.
- Related GH: runtime/pull/398 (kv-shard-hints) and runtime/pull/412 (tile-registry).

Last notes (informal)
--------------------
We're intentionally keeping the initial template set small to avoid combinatorial explosion. The runtime should learn which templates are useful and we can expand as we get telemetry. Prototype with 2 node shapes (NVLink-rich and PCIe-only) first.

Unresolved: If we can get RDMA-aware host aggregation primitives into the runtime, we can realize bigger wins for cross-host large-context traffic — need platform help.

----
Document draft, not final. Comments welcome.
